messages:
hari: seeing p99 token latency jitter on a satellite rack in apac-sg (rack-sat-07). GPU and CPU look fine but nic.tx_queue and softirq spikes line up with the blown p99s.
emma: which tenants? any single culprit?
rafa: top talker is t-211 but theres also bursty egress from a training job on t-199. combined they create packet-fanout and IRQ storm on the host.
marta: host syslog extract:
```
eth0: tx_queue_len=11840 tx_drops=276
kernel: softirq_sum=0.32 cpu=3
netdev: backlog=14000
```
hari: this is different from usual GPU-noisy neighbor—it's NIC-interference at the rack edge causing long tail in token send times for many small-response requests.
emma: fast mitigation: can we apply tenant-level egress caps and mark hosts as "egress-shield" so scheduler avoids packing more heavy-egress tasks there?
rafa: applied temporary policer pol-2021 to t-211 at 10 Mbps. also set host label egress-shield for rack-sat-07.
infra-bot: action taken: policer pol-2021 applied to tenant t-211; host label egress-shield set on rack-sat-07; monitoring p99.
emma: p99 fell from ~580ms to ~150ms in ~90s. good immediate win.
hari: longer-term proposal:
1) emit host.metric: egress_softirq_ratio and host.metric: tx_queue_len.
2) scheduler: decrease routing weight for hosts with softirq_ratio>0.25 && tx_queue_len>8k for 20m.
3) prefer routing heavy-egress tenants to regions with >NIC_headroom capacity.
rafa: cost note: migrating a noisy tenant off a 12-GPU dedicated slice costs ~0.5 GPU-hours/day in backfill; but frequent SLO misses cost more.
emma: agree. I'll draft the telemetry + small scheduler heuristic PR. Rafa, can you own the policer automation canary?
rafa: yep. will add a safety cutoff so we only auto-police when p99>SLO and host signals match.
marta: follow-up: if policer doesn't drop p99 within 10m, auto-soft-evict to sibling AZ and create incident.
infra-bot: incident created INC-2132 (sat-rack-nic-egress-interference). responders: hari,emma,rafa.
